rubric: PYTHON AS A FIRST LANGUAGE / THE STANDARD LIBRARY / CHAPTER 36

slides.title: Regular expressions
slides.main: A pattern describes a family of strings, not one string: “three digits, a hyphen, four digits.”

slides.title: Pattern basics
slides.main: search looks anywhere, match from the start, fullmatch the whole string.

body.text:
import re

print(bool(re.search(r"\d\d", "in the year 2024")))
print(re.search(r"c.t", "cat and cot").group())
print(re.match(r"\d+", "a123") is None, re.match(r"\d+", "123a").group())
print(bool(re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+", "hello")), bool(re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+", "Hello")))
print(bool(re.search(r"^a", "apple")), bool(re.search(r"e$", "apple")))

slides.title: Quantifiers and greediness
slides.main: Greediness causes half the surprises: add ? to get the minimum.

body.text: import re print(re.findall(r"\d{2,4}", "1 22 333 55555")) print(re.search(r"<.*>", "bold").group()) print(re.search(r"<.*?>", "bold").group()) print(re.findall(r"colou?r", "color colour colr"))

slides.title: Groups
slides.sub: Extract the pieces of text you need
slides.main: Groups are the main way to extract data, not just check it.

body.text:
import re

m = re.search(r"order (\d+) from (\d+)\.(\d+)", "order 123 from 05.03")
print(m.group(), m.group(1), m.groups(), m.span())
print(re.findall(r"(\w+)@(\w+)\.ru", "ivan@mail.ru, olga@ya.ru"))
for m in re.finditer(r"\d+", "a1 b22 c333"):
    print(m.group(), m.start())

slides.title: Named groups
slides.main: A name reads better than a number; use a non-capturing group when you need not remember.

body.text:
import re

pat = re.compile(r"(?P<y>\d{4})-(?P<m>\d\d)-(?P<d>\d\d)")
m = pat.search("date: 2024-03-05")
print(m["y"], m.group("m"), m.groupdict())
print(re.findall(r"(?:cat|dog)s?", "cats and dog, catalog"))

slides.title: sub and split
slides.sub: Replace and split by a pattern
slides.main: A replacement can use groups (\1) and even a function computing it.

body.text:
import re

print(re.sub(r"\s+", " ", "many   spaces\n here"))
print(re.sub(r"(\w+) (\w+)", r"\2 \1", "Ivan Petrov"))
print(re.sub(r"\d+", lambda m: str(int(m.group()) * 2), "5 apples and 12 pears"))
print(re.split(r"[,;]\s*", "a, b;c,  d"))
print(re.subn("a", "o", "ala"))

Petrov Ivan
10 apples and 24 pears

slides.title: Raw strings, compile, flags
slides.main: Verbose mode re.X is the best way to write a complex pattern: parts and notes.

body.text:
import re

print(len(r"\d"), len("\\d"))
pat = re.compile(r"""
    (\d{3})   # code
    -
    (\d{4})   # number
""", re.X)
print(pat.fullmatch("555-1234").groups())
print(re.findall(r"cat", "Cat CAT cat", re.I))
print(re.findall(r"^\w+", "one\ntwo\nthree", re.M))

slides.title: Boundaries and context checks
slides.main: Context checks are not in the result, but decide whether a match fits.

body.text:
import re

print(re.findall(r"\bcat\b", "cat cats catnip cat."))
print(re.findall(r"\d+(?=%)", "discount 20% and 5 pcs, 30%"))
print(re.findall(r"(?<=\$)\d+", "price $100 and 200"))
print(re.findall(r"\b(?!not)\w+", "not going, going"))

slides.title: Practice
slides.main: No perfect pattern exists for email or phone: a check only filters obvious garbage.

body.text:
import re

line = "2024-03-05 09:07:03 ERROR disk failure"
m = re.match(r"(?P<date>\S+) (?P<time>\S+) (?P<level>[A-Z]+) (?P<msg>.*)", line)
print(m.groupdict())
text = "mail: ivan@mail.ru, olga@ya.ru; tel. +7-900-123-45-67"
print(re.findall(r"[\w.]+@[\w.]+\w", text))
print(re.findall(r"\+7(?:-\d{2,3}){4}", text))

slides.title: Limits of regexes
slides.sub: Nesting is not for them; simple things need simple methods
slides.main: Do not parse HTML or JSON with them; avoid nested quantifiers: catastrophic backtracking.

body.text:
import re

print(re.search(r"<.+>", "<a><b>").group())
print(re.search(r"<[^>]+>", "<a><b>").group())
print("cat".startswith("c"), "cat" in "catalog", "a-b".replace("-", "+"))
Simple: startswith, in, replace. Regex: for variants, repeats, groups.

slides.title: Russian text
slides.main: `[а-я]` excludes `ё`; \d matches digits of other scripts: use [0-9] for plain ones.

body.text:
import re

print(re.findall(r"\w+", "Привет, мир! hello"))
print(re.findall(r"[а-я]+", "ёж и ель"))
print(re.findall(r"[а-яё]+", "ёж и ель"))
print(re.findall(r"\w+", "Привет hello", re.ASCII))
print(re.findall(r"[0-9]+", "123 ٣٤٥"), re.findall(r"\d+", "123 ٣٤٥"))

slides.title: Typical mistakes
slides.sub: None instead of a match, unescaped dot
slides.main: Check the search result before using a group; escape special characters with re.escape.

body.text:
import re

m = re.search(r"\d+", "no digits")
print(m)
print(re.search(r"1.5", "1x5") is not None, re.search(r"1\.5", "1x5") is not None)
print(re.escape("1.5+2"))
print(re.match(r"b", "abc"), re.search(r"b", "abc").group())
